title: PIR Over Wireless Channels: Achieving Privacy With Public Responses
extended_summary:
This paper addresses a communications-theory problem: private information retrieval (PIR) over a public additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channel, where server responses are visible to other servers and may leak the identity of the requested message. The authors focus on the privacy risk introduced by a wireless/shared-medium setting, which is not covered by earlier PIR work that assumed servers could not overhear each other’s responses.

To solve this, the paper proposes a joint PIR-channel coding scheme based on nested lattice codes and wiretap coset coding. The scheme is developed for both a two-server case and a general N-server case, including a block-fading AWGN multiple-access channel. The user sends carefully structured queries, servers encode linear combinations of messages, and the public transmissions are designed so the intended receiver can decode while a curious server cannot infer the desired index from overheard signals.

The paper is purely theoretical and does not study human participants, teachers, students, classrooms, or any educational intervention. Its main results are achievable PIR rate expressions showing that positive PIR rates remain possible even under public responses and, in the fading case, even when the malicious server’s channel can be stronger than the user’s. The authors also discuss secrecy and decoding conditions, along with scaling behavior as the number of servers increases.
